mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 0.3% in three months triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting investor concerns about labor market weakening.
regime_hint: rising unemployment in a labor market tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such instances are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or remain positive despite the UNRATE crossing threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices by >5% in the next month signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO increase by >5% in the next month
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day returns fail to outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a sustained 3-month rise in the CPIAUCSL index by >1% signals accelerating inflation expectations, prompting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >1% over the next 3 months in a late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: 20-day returns in such regimes are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or remain positive despite inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both demand (HOUST) and monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) by >0.5% in the next month signals accommodative policy, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and FEDFUNDS increase by >0.5% in the next month
failure_condition: 5-day returns fail to outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or remain negative despite the policy and demand convergence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in labor costs (PAYEMS) above 10,000 in the next month signals weakening labor market conditions, prompting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >10,000 in the next month
regime_hint: rising labor costs in an economic slowdown
failure_condition: 60-day returns in such instances are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or remain positive despite labor cost surges.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in demand (RSAFS) by >2% and rising unemployment (UNRATE) by >0.1% in the next month signals economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >2% while UNRATE rises by >0.1pp in the next month
regime_hint: tightening labor market with falling demand
failure_condition: 20-day returns in such instances are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or remain positive despite the demand and labor market divergence.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, simultaneous increases in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices by >5% in the next quarter signal economic normalization, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both INDPRO and GDPC1 increase by >5% in the next quarter
failure_condition: 5-day returns fail to outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or remain negative despite the supply and demand convergence in recovery.
